# Brainstorm: The Resilient Interaction Layer

> **Companion doc** to [`brainstorm.md`](./brainstorm.md) (platform) and
> [`browser_automation_brainstorm.md`](./browser_automation_brainstorm.md) (runtime, May 2026).
> This doc covers one layer in depth: **how Yantra's action-taking tools (click, fill,
> observe) behave on real-world pages, and how their results steer the orchestrating agent.**
> It supersedes the runtime doc's §6.3/§7.2 where they conflict, because the architecture has
> moved on since May: live agentic work (`do`) now runs an agent loop over direct,
> policy-wrapped tools (per `memory.md` Architecture), not plan-then-execute. The interaction
> layer is now the product's floor: every task type stands on it.

---

## Why this session exists

Several rounds of fixes have made individual click/fill cases work, yet real-world runs still
stumble. The decision driving this session: **stop patching symptom-by-symptom and design the
interaction layer as a system** — deliberate recovery model, deliberate result contract,
deliberate escalation path (including, possibly, vision) — while keeping simplicity at the
heart: recovery policy must not be interleaved with interaction business logic.

### Evidence: run `20260829T171218Z-do-0ae073f1` (2026-08-29, flight search DFW→SJC)

The run **completed and produced a genuinely good brief** — but the path there is the story:

- **792 s, 33 turns, 66 tool-call records, $0.23.** Of ~27 browser actions, 8 failed and 11
  more were the agent manually operating a date picker click-by-click.
- **`browser_fill_form` "Where from?" / "Where to?"** — `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` after 8.7–13.9 s
  each. All four typing strategies (fill, overtype, clear-then-type, native-setter) ran; the
  field "stayed empty" every time. Root cause (from the trace): the accessible name resolved to
  the **closed trigger control**, while the page hands keystrokes to a **different input inside
  the overlay it opens**. Every retry rung varied _how_ to type into the wrong node; none asked
  _where_ the keystrokes were landing. When the agent later targeted the overlay input by ref
  (`e80`) directly, the same engine immediately produced suggestion candidates.
- **The retype trap.** `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` correctly reported three offered labels and
  advised _"re-issue this call with one of those strings exactly as written."_ The agent
  obeyed — and typing the full label `"San Jose Mineta International Airport (SJC)"` into a
  prefix-matching autocomplete yielded **zero suggestions**, a cleared field, and a 13.9 s
  `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED`. The tool's own recovery advice steered the agent into a dead end,
  because no engine path exists that makes that advice work.
- **Date fill collapse.** `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE`: _"No date widget driver recognized
  'Departure' with sufficient confidence."_ The drivers detect from closed state only (a sound
  no-side-effects rule), but a bare textbox trigger that only reveals its calendar on click is
  invisible to closed-state detection. The attached hint — _"check details.displayedMonths or
  details.offered"_ — referenced payload fields that were **absent**, because hints are keyed
  by error code while the same code arises from unrelated causes. The agent then drove the
  calendar by hand: **11 click turns** (~35 s wall, plus LLM latency and tokens) doing exactly
  what a calendar driver exists to do in one call.
- **Copy hygiene.** `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` said _"The run is out of exploration time. Publish now
  using the evidence already gathered. Publish your result now with the evidence you already
  gathered — it is attached automatically."_ — the same instruction twice, because
  [budget.ts:196](../packages/agent/src/runtime/budget.ts#L196) already carries the remedy for
  the soft wall-clock limit and [middleware.ts:253-255](../packages/agent/src/runtime/middleware.ts#L253)
  appends a second one unconditionally. Small, but the agent reads every character.
  _(Correction, verified 2026-08-29: an earlier draft of this doc also reported a mojibake
  em-dash. That was a read artifact — Windows PowerShell 5.1 defaults `Get-Content` to ANSI.
  The byte stream holds a correct U+2014; there is no encoding bug. Only the duplication is
  real.)_
- **What worked and must be kept** (validated by the same run):
  - Evidence-gated navigation (`URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE`) refused two fabricated URLs, and the
    _second_ refusal escalated with specific alternative moves. Textbook steering.
  - `requested` / `committed` / `resolution` semantics — a widget resolving "DFW" to "Dallas"
    reads as an answer, not a failure (the lesson already captured in `memory.md`).
  - Offered-labels on ambiguity, attempt ledgers ("already tried X — don't repeat"),
    release-before-verify, in-call budgets, post-action observation in every result.

### The diagnosis, in one paragraph

The engine's recovery is deep but **one-dimensional**. All rungs vary the _mechanics_ of the
same act on the same node. Real-world widget failures live on three independent axes — **WHERE**
(is this live node actually the editee?), **WHAT** (what query/value shape does this widget
respond to?), and **HOW** (typing mechanics, pacing, native setters) — and the current ladder
only climbs HOW. Meanwhile the results layer, which is genuinely well-designed, has one
structural gap: hints are attached per error code rather than per cause, so a failure can carry
another failure's advice, and advice is not guaranteed to correspond to any engine capability.
Everything below follows from those two sentences.

---

## Design principles (proposed as standing rules for this layer)

1. **Interaction protocols, not element actions.** Real pages speak a small number of widget
   protocols: plain text, type-ahead/combobox, option list, date (input or calendar), toggle
   group, composite range. Tools express _semantic intent_; protocol drivers own the
   conversation with the widget, including its multi-step choreography. An agent manually
   paging a calendar is, by definition, a missing/failed driver — never an acceptable
   steady state.
2. **Recovery varies the question, not just the attempt.** Every recovery rung is typed by
   axis — WHERE / WHAT / HOW — and carries an entry condition based on evidence from prior
   rungs. Evidence that says "keystrokes are not landing here" must divert to the WHERE axis,
   not fund two more HOW rungs. Corollary: fast-fail is a feature — a fill that cannot work
   should say so in ~4 s, not 14 s.
3. **Recovery is data, not control flow.** Today recovery lives in at least four nested layers
   (tool `driveWithRetry` → `withAttempts` → engine-internal re-acquisition → typing ladder →
   reaction watcher). Each is individually principled; the composition is hard to reason about
   and produced artifacts like a `native-setter` attempt recording `errorCode: null` inside an
   overall failure. Proposal: per protocol family, **one declarative escalation plan** (an
   ordered list of typed rungs: axis, entry condition, cost cap, evidence produced) executed by
   **one runner** that owns budgets and the ledger. Business logic stays in rungs; policy stays
   in the plan; the ledger falls out for free. New fallbacks become a plan edit, not a new
   wrapper.
4. **The page is the oracle.** Never assume where typing lands, what a widget accepts, or
   whether an action took — ask the DOM (focus, value deltas, `aria-activedescendant`,
   suggestion lists, post-action mutations). This is also what keeps everything site-generic
   per the standing rule: structural signals only.
5. **A turn is the most expensive resource.** In-call recovery costs milliseconds; a failed
   tool call costs an LLM turn (seconds, tokens, and a chance to go off-course). Spend
   generous in-call budget _when evidence says progress is being made_, and return early when
   it says the axis is wrong. Track **turns-spent-compensating** as the layer's north-star
   metric.
6. **Results are steering, and hints are contracts.** The agent does exactly what results
   suggest (this run proves it — both for good and for the retype trap). Therefore: **a hint
   may only name a move the engine has a dedicated path for.** If the result says "re-issue
   with one of the offered strings", re-issuing an offered string must hit a fast path that is
   engineered to succeed. Advice without a corresponding capability is a bug class.

---

## Proposals

### Wave 1 — the failure classes this run exposed

- **P1. Type-ahead/combobox becomes a first-class widget family.** Today "typeahead" is an
  emergent behavior of `commitText` + `watchAndSelect` inside the engine; date and option get
  drivers, but the single most failure-prone real-world widget does not. A combobox driver
  gets: closed-state detection (`role=combobox`, `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-haspopup=listbox`,
  editable-with-linked-popup shapes), ownership of the **trigger → overlay → real editee**
  choreography, query shaping (P3), suggestion settling, ranking, selection, and commit
  verification against the chosen option. This one driver absorbs the "Where from?/Where to?"
  class wholesale.
- **P2. Editee resolution (the WHERE rung).** After engaging a target, send one probe
  keystroke and ask the page where it landed: did `document.activeElement` move, did any
  visible editable's value change, did `aria-activedescendant` appear? If the editee is a
  different live node, re-target the rest of the drive to it (and report the substitution in
  the result, tie-break-style). Generic by construction — it reads observed focus and value
  flow, never site shape. This turns the run's three 9–14 s failures into one success.
- **P3. Query shaping for type-aheads (the WHAT rung).** One ordered query plan per fill:
  as-given → code-style token (an uppercase 3-letter token like "SJC" is _already_ partially
  handled by the code-to-label fixture — unify it here) → **prefix retreat** (when the full
  value yields zero suggestions, retreat to a shortened distinguishing prefix and rank the
  suggestions against the _full_ requested value). Prefix retreat is what makes P4's contract
  honest, and it kills the retype trap.
- **P4. The actionable-hint invariant.** Every hint template in the result layer must map to a
  named engine capability, enforced by a test that enumerates hint templates and asserts the
  corresponding path exists and is exercised. Concretely: "re-issue with an offered string"
  requires a **select-by-offered-label fast path** (type the distinguishing prefix, click the
  matching option — never naive full-label retype).
- **P5. Hints keyed by (code, cause), not by code.** Keep `error_code` stable for programmatic
  handling; add a `cause` discriminator (e.g. `NOT_COMMITTED/keystrokes-landed-elsewhere` vs
  `NOT_COMMITTED/value-rejected-on-release`; `TARGET_UNREACHABLE/driver-not-recognized` vs
  `TARGET_UNREACHABLE/value-not-offered`). Message + hint + details schema are selected by the
  pair. This makes the standing memory rule — two failures sharing a code must not read
  identically — structural, and fixes the wrong-hint bug (a "check displayedMonths" hint on a
  failure that has no months to check).
- **P6. Engine-owned open-probe stage.** Keep the driver rule "detection never clicks" — it's
  what makes detection safe to run broadly. Add a distinct, engine-owned stage that runs when
  closed-state confidence is low but field semantics are strong (name/placeholder/value smells
  like a date; intent is a date): open the widget once (click the trigger), re-run detection
  against the open state, then drive — or dismiss and fail with what was actually seen. One
  bounded probe, evidence recorded in the ledger. This converts "no driver recognized
  'Departure'" + 11 manual clicks into a single driven fill.
- **P7. `browser_fill_form` partial-progress semantics.** Independent fields continue after
  one fails; the batch result reports three explicit sets — `applied` (with per-field
  committed/resolution), `failed` (with per-field cause), `remaining` (skipped because
  genuinely dependent on a failed field). The current behavior — abort the batch on field one,
  `applied: []`, message about only that field — wastes the batch's whole reason to exist and
  hides state from the agent.

### Wave 2 — systemic hardening

- **P8. Declarative escalation plans** (per principle 3): migrate the existing nested
  retry/ladder layers onto the rung/plan/runner model, starting by expressing the _current_
  behavior as a plan (no behavior change), then adding the WHERE/WHAT rungs from Wave 1. The
  combobox family (P1) is built on this model from day one and proves it; date/option migrate
  after.
- **P9. Obstruction protocol for clicks and fills.** On hit-target interception or a fill
  whose target is covered: classify the obstruction from structure (`aria-modal` dialog,
  fixed/sticky overlay, spinner), attempt one bounded generic clearance when the obstructing
  subtree offers an obvious dismiss control (`aria-label` close, visible "decline/close"
  button _inside the obstructing subtree_), otherwise fail with the obstruction described and
  its dismiss candidates offered as refs. No site-specific dismissal tables, ever.
- **P10. Page-delta observation in results.** Post-action results carry a compact delta
  (URL change, dialog opened/closed, N elements appeared/vanished, focus moved) alongside or
  instead of the full observation block. Cheaper in tokens, and more _salient_ — "a dialog
  named 'Search results' opened" steers better than 80 re-listed elements. Full observation
  stays available via `browser_observe`.
- **P11. Result copy hygiene as a tested surface.** Golden-message tests per (code, cause)
  pair: assert distinct wording, no duplicated sentences, no encoding artifacts, no hint
  referencing absent detail fields, ledger entries never carry `errorCode: null` inside an
  overall failure (record a per-rung verdict instead: what was learned). The agent reads every
  character; messages are a product surface and deserve tests like one.
- **P12. The Widget Gauntlet.** A local fixture gallery of _generic adversarial widget
  patterns_, each distilled from a real failure but encoding only structure (the existing
  `code-to-label-typeahead.html` fixture is the seed): portal-overlay combobox with detached
  editee; re-mounting search form; slow suggestions (>1.5 s); prefix-only matcher; masked
  input; split date fields; shared-calendar range pair; virtualized listbox; consent modal
  obstruction; sticky-header hit interception; shadow-DOM select. CI runs the full interaction
  layer against the gauntlet on every change, reporting the metrics below. Site names appear
  only in fixture comments as provenance, per the standing rule.

### Measurable goals (what "solid" means)

| Metric                                                                                 | Today (evidence run) | Target                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Turns spent compensating for tool gaps (manual widget-cranking, retry-after-misadvice) | ~14 of 33            | **0–2**                                            |
| Wall time for this task class                                                          | 13.2 min             | **≤ 4 min**                                        |
| Failed fill answers in                                                                 | 8.7–13.9 s           | **≤ 4 s** (unless evidence shows in-call progress) |
| Hints that name an engineered path                                                     | partial              | **100% (tested)**                                  |
| Distinct (code, cause) messages                                                        | code-keyed           | **pair-keyed (golden-tested)**                     |
| Gauntlet pass rate                                                                     | n/a                  | tracked per fixture, gating                        |

## Vision assist: the opt-in screenshot tool

### Positioning

The industry has split: vision-first agents (OpenAI Operator/CUA) buy generality with
variance, cost, and privacy exposure; accessibility-tree-first agents (Playwright MCP,
Yantra today) are cheap, deterministic, and sanitizable — and struggle in exactly the places
this run struggled, where the a11y tree misrepresents what a sighted user sees (overlay
comboboxes, visual date grids, obscured controls). Browser-Use's trajectory (text-first,
vision as fallback) suggests the hybrid is the pragmatic frontier. **Yantra's angle:
deterministic-first, vision as a bounded, consent-gated evidence channel — never the primary
control loop.** The screenshot never drives; it helps the agent decide which deterministic
tool call to make next. That keeps the "small model orchestrating predictable tools" bet
intact.

### Consent model (aligned with standing memory rules)

- **Explicit grant, asked once, stored** — mirroring the established grant pattern for
  sensitive context. Vision assist is _off_ until the user grants it; the grant is a saved
  artifact (profile-scoped preference), not a per-invocation opt-in flag; a negation override
  (`--no-screenshots`) exists for one-run suppression, consistent with the flag vocabulary
  rule.
- **The warning is loud and specific, because nothing is masked.** At grant time (and in docs):
  _screenshots are raw, unmasked pixels of whatever the page shows — including logged-in
  content, names, balances, and messages — and are sent to the configured model provider._
  The text sanitizer cannot see into pixels; the user must understand they are opting out of
  that guarantee for image payloads. Local-model providers (Ollama) soften but don't remove
  the warning.
- **Structurally blocked where LLMs are blocked.** Scheduled/daemon runs and nested
  `workflow_run` are hard zero-LLM; the screenshot tool must not exist there regardless of
  grant. Secret-bearing steps should also refuse capture while a resolved secret could be
  on-screen (e.g. between secret fill and submit) — a cheap, generic guard.
- **Fully audited.** Every capture is saved to `runs/<id>/screenshots/`, referenced from
  `tool-calls.jsonl`, and surfaced by `yantra audit` as "the model saw these images." The
  user can open exactly what the model saw. Captures are size-bounded (dimensions, format,
  per-run count) and count against run budget.

### Mechanics (proposed)

- **`browser_screenshot` as an agent-requested tool**, described to the agent as _fallback
  evidence when text observation is insufficient or contradicts behavior_ — viewport capture,
  optionally element-scoped. Start agent-requested only; auto-attach-on-repeated-failure is a
  possible later config, but agent-requested keeps every capture visible as a deliberate,
  audited decision.
- **Set-of-marks overlay.** Before capture, draw the current observation's `eNN` ref labels
  onto the image (our own annotation of our own capture). The model can then bind pixels to
  refs directly — "the control you want is `e80`" — which is precisely the WHERE information
  the text channel kept getting wrong. This is the highest-leverage 20% of vision for
  Yantra's architecture.
- **Where it plausibly rescues real runs** (from this session's evidence classes): overlay
  comboboxes whose editee the a11y tree obscures; date grids whose month/day layout is
  visual; obstruction disputes ("the tool says clicked, nothing happened"); "which of these
  same-named controls" ambiguity; CAPTCHAs and interstitials (recognize and hand off, never
  solve — consistent with ethics rules).

---

## Risks

- **Recovery-model refactor destabilizes what works.** The current layer embeds hard-won
  lessons in comments and behavior. → Mitigation: P8 first expresses current behavior as a
  plan with zero behavior change, gated by the gauntlet + existing suites; lessons move from
  comments into named rungs and fixtures.
- **Open-probe side effects.** Probing (clicking a trigger) can mutate page state (open a
  dialog that traps focus). → Mitigation: probe only when intent and field semantics align,
  single probe per fill, always followed by drive-or-dismiss; ledger records it.
- **Vision scope creep.** The screenshot channel quietly becomes the primary loop ("just look
  at the page"), eroding determinism, cost, and privacy properties. → Mitigation: capture
  budget per run, tool description frames it as fallback evidence, metrics track
  captures-per-run, and the deterministic gauntlet must keep passing with vision disabled —
  the layer may never _require_ sight.
- **Gauntlet overfitting.** Fixtures drift toward "sites we've seen" rather than structures.
  → Mitigation: fixture review checks that each encodes a nameable generic pattern; site
  names in comments only.

## Open questions (for the user, then the Planner)

1. **Refactor scope for recovery-as-data (P8):** incremental (combobox family proves the
   model, date/option migrate later — recommended) vs. one migration pass?
2. **Screenshot grant scope:** per-profile (recommended — matches trusted-host philosophy and
   keeps authenticated profiles deliberate) vs. global? And is grant revocation a `yantra`
   command surface in the same release?
3. **Auto-attach screenshots on repeated failure** — ever, or agent-requested forever?
   (Recommended: agent-requested only until real runs show the extra step matters.)
4. **`fill_form` dependency semantics (P7):** is "continue independent fields, skip dependent
   ones" the right default, and how is dependence declared/inferred (document order after a
   failed field on the same widget group)?
5. **Delta-vs-full observation (P10):** does the agent prompt need both available, or does
   delta replace the embedded observation in action results entirely?
